newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC May profits rise as crude costs fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC May profits rise as crude costs fall.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Tuesday its May pre-tax profit was T$2.559 billion compared with T$2.003 billion in April.
An oil monopoly official reached by telephone attributed the rise in profits mainly to falling crude import costs.
Chinese Petroleum's May oil import costs averaged US$17.76 per barrel, higher than the $15.26 budgeted for the period but lower than April's US$18.74, company figures showed.

The company raised oil prices an average nine percent on January 1 and a further 2.97 percent on April 4, saying more income was needed despite a general decline in world crude prices to whittle away a growing fiscal budget deficit.
Against the backdrop of falling crude prices, the increases also helped to boost profits, the official said.
As of May, Chinese Petroleum had accumulated a deficit of T$15.196 billion from the current fiscal year ending June 30.
